statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: The level cap is 60, and Blizzard plans horizontal progression rather than raising it.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: The 1–60 XP curve is unchanged from Classic, about 4,084,700 XP in total. Examples: 27,600 XP to reach level 10, 1,154,400 XP to reach 40, and 209,800 XP for level 59→60.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: There is no global XP multiplier. An earlier claim that the curve differs from Classic was retracted.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: There is no level scaling in the open world.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: More than 1,000 new quests span levels 1–60.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: Mob level colours: grey means no XP. Green is 3–4 levels below you, yellow within 2, orange 3–4 above, red 5+ above.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: Quests more than 5 levels below you lose part of their XP for each further level.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: Grouped kill XP: in a 5-player group each member gets the kill XP ÷ 5 × 1.4 (100 XP solo becomes 28 XP each). Quest turn-in XP is not reduced by grouping. Raids get no credit for quest objectives.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: Kill XP for each player is based on that player's own level, as in Classic Era (a bug fixed on 2026-10-08).

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: Tagging: the first player or group to damage a mob owns the kill. Party members must be alive and nearby to share credit.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: DoTs tag instantly, so opening with a DoT wins contested tags.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: Exploring new areas gives a small amount of XP.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: Hotfixes removed kill XP from Shatterspear Trolls (Nov 10) and quest XP from the repeatable "Water Pouch Bounty" (Nov 16), closing farming loops.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: At level 60 quests are not converted to gold. Instead, most quests of level 48 and above now also reward gold (Nov 10 hotfix). Quests that already reward valuable items, repeatables and trivial quests are excluded.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: Higher-level mob health was raised to offset broad class damage buffs. No numbers were given.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: Respawns are fastest in starting zones and slow down as you level. Blizzard said it would slow low-level respawns once the launch rush ends.

statements.title: XP mechanics in Forever (scope: forever)
statements.text: Blizzard's design target for solo play: an ordinary mob should take about 10–15 seconds to kill.

statements.title: XP formulas (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Grey level: levels 1–5 have none. For levels 6–39 it is L − floor(L/10) − 5. For levels 40–59 it is L − floor(L/5) − 1. Examples: at 20 grey is 13, at 30 it is 22, at 40 it is 31, at 50 it is 39.

statements.title: XP formulas (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Base mob XP = level × 5 + 45. Each level the mob is above you adds 5%, capped at about +4 levels. XP falls linearly to zero at the grey level. Elites give 2× XP.

statements.title: XP formulas (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Green mobs give only slightly less XP than yellow ones but die faster and more safely, so grinding greens is efficient.

statements.title: XP formulas (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Quest XP is full until you are more than 5 levels above the quest. It then falls to 80% at +6, 60% at +7, 40% at +8, 20% at +9 and 10% at +10 or more.

statements.title: XP formulas (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Group modifiers by party size: 1 or 2 players ×1.0, 3 ×1.166, 4 ×1.3, 5 ×1.4 (best-guess values).

statements.title: XP formulas (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Quest XP is a shrinking share of each level as you climb (about 10.7% of a level per quest at level 5, about 3% at 59). Later levels depend more on kills.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Design intent: dungeon kill XP cut sharply and dungeon-quest XP raised a lot, to keep players in the open world. No numbers.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Only the *extra* XP dungeon quests gave above a normal quest was halved, not the whole quest reward.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Dungeon kill XP raised by about 20%.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Developers stated that repeat dungeon runs should get close to optimal questing but never beat it.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: XP values were adjusted on various quests, with no dungeon numbers given. All Ruins of Lordaeron quests now require level 15.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: All dungeon kill XP +50%, compared only with the previous Forever value. Listed in the Nov 9 hotfix notes.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: If an enemy was trivial (grey) to any party member, nobody in the party got kill XP from it. This broke normal groups, e.g. level-34 trash in Razorfen Downs.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Revised rule: party kill XP is cancelled only when a party member is more than 12 levels above the enemy (a gap of exactly 12 still gives XP). Instances already in progress keep the old rule until reset.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Strategy consensus: one clear per dungeon at the right level with every quest for it in your log, then return to questing. Farming one instance after its quests are done is not worth it.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Bringing a much higher-level friend gives the whole party zero kill XP (rule 8), so old-style "boost runs" are over.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Examples of dungeon-quest XP, Forever vs Classic: one Wailing Caverns quest 3,100 vs 1,600; the Deadmines quest set 18,450 vs 8,300; City of Dalaran quests about 15,800 per faction. Values may have changed since.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Measured quest totals: Ruins of Lordaeron about 29.8k (Horde, levels 16–18); Excavation Site about 39.3k with 7 quests (Alliance) or about 22.8k with 4 (Horde); City of Dalaran about 37.6k; Gnomeregan about 54k (Alliance, 12 quests). Nothing above level 30 has been measured.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Estimates of dungeon kill XP versus Classic are all unofficial and range from about 24% to 55% of Classic.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Non-boss mobs in The Drowned City respawn after 2 h (was 1 h; Nov 13). A bug that gave Drowned City mobs 30% too much damage was fixed on Nov 9.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Pix Xizzix offers weekly dungeon quests, which are removed at the weekly reset.

statements.title: Dungeon XP rules and timeline (scope: forever)
statements.text: Several quest drops are now shared with every eligible party member (e.g. Deadwood Key, Venom-dripping Heart, Croaky's Head).

statements.title: Dungeon list, level ranges and value by level (scope: forever)
statements.text: Run each dungeon near the top of its range with every quest for it. Collect the quests and pre-quests a level or two early. If a group is more than about 20 minutes from forming, keep questing instead.

statements.title: Dungeon list, level ranges and value by level (scope: forever)
statements.text: No automatic matchmaking: the Group Finder is a listing, and meeting stones can't summon. Quests that start from an item can't be shared, so every player needs their own item and pre-quests.

statements.title: Dungeon list, level ranges and value by level (scope: forever)
statements.text: Suggested Alliance stops: Hall of Thanes 14–17 (5 quests), Deadmines 18–22 (9 quests), BFD 23–26 (once), Stockade 25–29 (only if you have its quests), Excavation Site 27–30 (11+ quests), Dalaran 30–33 (8 quests, after the key chain), Gnomeregan 30+ (about 12 quests), Drowned City 35–40 (once, alongside the Stranglethorn quests), Uldaman early 40s, Krol'dok 40–45 (9 quests, about 61.5k XP claimed), Alcaz 50–53, Blackmaw 57–60, Shaper's Terrace 58–60. Scarlet Monastery is weak for Alliance.

statements.title: Dungeon list, level ranges and value by level (scope: forever)
statements.text: Suggested Horde stops: Ragefire Chasm 13–15 (once, 5 quests), Ruins of Lordaeron 17–19 (described as one of the best runs, but hard below 17), Wailing Caverns 18–22, Shadowfang Keep 22–25 (optional, best for Undead), Razorfen Kraul 29+ (optional), Razorfen Downs (once).

statements.title: Dungeon list, level ranges and value by level (scope: forever)
statements.text: Both factions: Zul'Farrak, Maraudon, Sunken Temple and Blackrock Depths are worthwhile, and Blackrock Depths has the most quests. Dire Maul, Scholomance and Stratholme are endgame, not levelling stops.

statements.title: Dungeon list, level ranges and value by level (scope: forever)
statements.text: Blizzard restored Upper Blackrock Spire's health and damage to intended values on Nov 17.

statements.title: Classic dungeon ranges, "recommended" convention (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Warcraft Tavern's Classic recommended ranges are narrower than the group finder ranges: RFC 13–18, Deadmines 15–22, WC 17–24, SFK 20–26, BFD 22–28, Stockade 25–29, RFK 29–34, Gnomeregan 30–35, SM Graveyard 30–34, Library 30–36, Armory 32–38, Cathedral 35–45, Uldaman 36–45, RFD 38–42, ZF 40–47, Maraudon 45–51, Sunken Temple 50–55, BRD 52–60, LBRS 57–60.

statements.title: Classic dungeon ranges, "recommended" convention (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: In Classic, quests run thin around level 50, and 57–60 was mostly dungeon quests plus grinding. Forever adds content at 50–60 (Hyjal, Blackmaw, Shaper's Terrace, Alcaz), so this may no longer hold.

statements.title: Classic dungeon ranges, "recommended" convention (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: In Classic, dungeon boosting and waiting at the entrance were often optimal. Forever deliberately discourages both.

statements.title: Rested XP, camping, XP buffs and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: Rested XP builds at 5% of the current level per 8 hours in a rested area (inn, capital city). The cap is 150% of a level, about 10 days of resting.

statements.title: Rested XP, camping, XP buffs and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: Rested XP doubles kill XP only. Quest and exploration XP do not use it up.

statements.title: Rested XP, camping, XP buffs and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: The Legacy talent Well Rested (Adventure tree, 5 ranks) adds 4% per rank to both the rested build-up rate and the cap, up to +20%.

statements.title: Rested XP, camping, XP buffs and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: The Camp Tent (a Leatherworking camp feature) raises rested XP by 5% of a level, and does nothing if you already have more than that. Camp features share a 1-hour cooldown, and you must stay at the camp for at least a minute.
The Journeyman Campfire Kit needs Cooking 90 to place since 10 Nov (was 140).

statements.title: Rested XP, camping, XP buffs and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: The campfire buff works while sitting, sleeping, lying down or kneeling, and while casting or crafting.

statements.title: Rested XP, camping, XP buffs and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: Campfires no longer damage players below level 5. "Boosted Rest" is a camping debuff.

statements.title: Rested XP, camping, XP buffs and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: The Cozy Sleeping Bag comes from a quest chain starting around level 14 (Barrens or Westfall). It gives +1% XP per stack up to 3 stacks (+3%), lasts about 2 hours and persists through death. Sources disagree on how the stacks build.

statements.title: Rested XP, camping, XP buffs and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: Since the Nov 17 hotfix the Cozy Sleeping Bag shows a Resting aura inside its area, and players can no longer sleep on it while mounted.

statements.title: Rested XP, camping, XP buffs and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: Most cooked food gives Well Fed: +5% kill XP for about 15 minutes, lost on death, stacking with the camp and sleeping-bag buffs, and working in dungeons.

statements.title: Rested XP, camping, XP buffs and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: Session habit: always log out in an inn or capital, and bind your hearthstone to the hub you will start from next session.

statements.title: Rested XP, camping, XP buffs and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: Rested XP mainly benefits characters that spend time offline. Park alts in a city early to build rest.

statements.title: Rested XP, camping, XP buffs and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: One guide suggests spending banked rest at 40–60, where each level needs the most XP. This is an opinion.

statements.title: Rested XP details (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Logging out outside a rested area builds rest at one quarter of the normal rate. No Forever source states this.

statements.title: Rested XP details (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Logout is instant in a rested area and takes 20 seconds elsewhere. The portrait glows while you are resting.

statements.title: Rested XP details (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Gathering herbs and ore gives XP, doubled while rested. This is described for retail and is unverified for Classic and Forever.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: Polestar plans routes with these priorities, in order: (1) safety: keep solo players off mobs 2 or more levels above them (+1 gets a warning) and route around non-group elites; (2) flow: no backtracking, hand in when the route passes the quest giver, pick up quests early if they finish on a later visit, and fit class training into stops already made; (3) quests over grinding: fill XP gaps with quests from any reachable zone, keep grinding to short top-ups, and suggest a fitting dungeon at grind steps; (4) raw time last.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: Polestar's simulation uses the hearthstone about once an hour, never while it is on cooldown, and only when it saves a long trip. Flights go only to flight paths you have learned. Boats, zeppelins, the tram and portals run on real timetables.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: Polestar keeps dungeon, raid and PvP quests out of the main route. Elite and group quests stay in, each with a solo alternative. Rare-drop quests are optional. With "skip grey quests" on, it drops grey or low-XP quests you have left behind unless a later quest needs them, and always keeps quests that give full XP.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: Batch a hub: pick up all of its quests, do them in a single loop, turn them all in at once.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: Bind the hearthstone at inns near busy quest areas and pick up every flight path you pass.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: The Legacy talent Frequent Flier makes flights cheaper and faster. Guides say flight costs are halved and the flight mount is 20% faster; the official article gives no numbers.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: New boats: Stormwind Harbor to Auberdine; a Southshore stop on the Auberdine–Menethil loop (sources disagree on the sailing direction); a neutral boat from Tanaris to Powderfuse Port in Riverglades.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: Classic transport is unchanged: Menethil–Theramore, Rut'theran–Auberdine, Feathermoon–Forgotten Coast, the Deeprun Tram, Horde zeppelins from Orgrimmar to Undercity and Grom'gol and from Undercity to Grom'gol, and the Ratchet–Booty Bay boat. There are no flying mounts.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: Before level 40 everyone travels on foot, apart from Druid and Shaman travel forms and the Tauren Plainsrunning speed bonus (up to 60% speed, not while mounted).

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: Skyborne Alliance characters reportedly have a Skyborne-only portal from Dalaran to Stormwind. Not verified in game.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: Leaving a dungeon group teleports you to your hearthstone location even when the stone is on cooldown. Whether this is intended, and so usable as a free hearth, is unverified.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: Route guides save time mainly by cutting the time spent looking for NPCs and quests. No measured saving has been published.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: RestedXP's Forever routes cover levels 1–35. Above 35 the addon falls back to its Classic Era routes.

statements.title: Route efficiency, hand-in batching, hearthstone, flight paths and travel (scope: forever)
statements.text: Other Forever route addons exist: Leveldon (1–30), Navryk (1–30), RouteXP (Horde 30–60), Shortest Path Forever and Factoruide (which feeds Polestar).

statements.title: Classic speed-route habits (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Finish everything in your quest log for an area before returning to town, and drop quests that need a long detour.

statements.title: Classic speed-route habits (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Accept only the quests your route uses, to keep log space free.

statements.title: Classic speed-route habits (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Kill mobs that are on your path between objectives, to cut later grinding.

statements.title: Classic speed-route habits (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Hearthstone philosophy is split. Joana/Nightfall-style routes re-bind only at planned points and save the stone for planned returns. Others re-bind in every zone and use it whenever it is ready. Polestar (Forever) takes the first approach.

statements.title: Classic speed-route habits (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Fly to a capital only once several hand-ins have piled up, and chain quests across zones to avoid backtracking.

statements.title: Classic speed-route habits (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Abandon quests that need a cross-zone trip for only one or two hand-ins.

statements.title: When to skip or abandon quests (scope: forever)
statements.text: Skip grey quests unless they unlock a later quest in a chain. Polestar implements exactly this rule.

statements.title: When to skip or abandon quests (scope: forever)
statements.text: Green quests still give full XP, so do not skip them for their colour. This is a Classic mechanic that Forever also describes.

statements.title: When to skip or abandon quests (scope: forever)
statements.text: Orange and red quests lower your hit chance and raise downtime and repair costs. Wait until they are yellow or green, or do them with a partner. If a fight brings you close to death, the quest is probably above your level.

statements.title: When to skip or abandon quests (scope: forever)
statements.text: Open-world elites hit hard. Follow the quest's group recommendation.

statements.title: When to skip or abandon quests (scope: forever)
statements.text: Don't skip quests because their Classic rewards were poor. Forever improved many quest rewards.

statements.title: When to skip or abandon quests (scope: forever)
statements.text: There is no reason to save quests for level 60, since 60 gives no XP-to-gold conversion. Quests of level 48 and above already pay gold.

statements.title: When to skip or abandon quests (scope: forever)
statements.text: Dungeon quests are worth collecting in advance (see KB-G03 #1), even though Polestar leaves them out of the solo route.

statements.title: Starting zones per race (scope: forever)
statements.text: Polestar's starting-zone routes: Human, Elwynn 1–11. Dwarf and Gnome, Dun Morogh 1–14. Night Elf, Teldrassil 1–13 then Darkshore 12–15. Skyborne, Zephras Isle 1–15. Orc and Troll, Durotar 1–12. Tauren, Mulgore 1–13. Undead, Tirisfal 1–13.

statements.title: Starting zones per race (scope: forever)
statements.text: Zephras Isle is the neutral 1–12 starting zone for the new Skyborne race.

statements.title: Starting zones per race (scope: forever)
statements.text: The Skyborne airship drops Alliance characters in northern Dalaran (Alterac Mountains) and Horde characters at Skywatcher Plateau in north-west Mulgore.

statements.title: Starting zones per race (scope: forever)
statements.text: After Zephras Isle, RestedXP sends Skyborne Alliance to Westfall and Skyborne Horde to Silverpine or the Barrens.

statements.title: Starting zones per race (scope: forever)
statements.text: New quests per starting zone (beta count): Teldrassil 11, Elwynn 8, Tirisfal 14 plus 8 Paladin-only, Durotar 13, Mulgore 9.

statements.title: Starting zones per race (scope: forever)
statements.text: RestedXP sends Night Elves to Loch Modan at levels 14–16.

statements.title: Starting zones per race (scope: forever)
statements.text: All Alliance races then join one shared route beginning in Westfall, and all Horde races one shared route through Silverpine and the Barrens.

statements.title: Alliance zone order 10–60 (scope: forever)
statements.text: Polestar's Alliance route crosses between continents several times: boat to Auberdine around 15, back to the Eastern Kingdoms around 18, Darkshore again at 21–23, Ashenvale and Stonetalon at 22–25, Dustwallow and Thousand Needles at 31–33, and Desolace at 33–35 and 38–39.

statements.title: Alliance zone order 10–60 (scope: forever)
statements.text: A shop-run guide's outline: Westfall, Loch Modan or Darkshore 12–18; Redridge and the end of Westfall 18–21; Wetlands 21–25; Duskwood and Ashenvale 24–27; Wetlands, Hillsbrad and Duskwood 27–30; from 30 the zones are shared with Horde.

statements.title: Alliance zone order 10–60 (scope: forever)
statements.text: Simulated time to 60 on Polestar's Alliance route is about 127.5 hours /played, including rested XP.

statements.title: Horde zone order 10–60 (scope: forever)
statements.text: Polestar's Horde route crosses between continents: Barrens around 14, back to the Eastern Kingdoms at 22–25 (Hillsbrad), Kalimdor again at 24–29, then Stranglethorn from 33.

statements.title: Horde zone order 10–60 (scope: forever)
statements.text: A shop-run guide's outline: Barrens/Crossroads or Silverpine 12–16; northern Barrens 16–21; the end of the Barrens then Stonetalon 21–25; Ashenvale 25–28; Thousand Needles 28–30.

statements.title: Horde zone order 10–60 (scope: forever)
statements.text: Horde players coming from Kalimdor can reach Riverglades by the Tanaris boat.

statements.title: Horde zone order 10–60 (scope: forever)
statements.text: Simulated time to 60 on Polestar's Horde route is about 120.9 hours /played, including rested XP.

statements.title: Horde zone order 10–60 (scope: forever)
statements.text: A Joana-derived Classic Horde route runs Durotar 1–12, Barrens 12–14 with a trip to Thunder Bluff, then Barrens 15–19 with side trips to Ashenvale and Stonetalon. Its shape is the same as Polestar's (classic_fallback).

statements.title: Zone level ranges and new zones (scope: forever)
statements.text: Forever adds four zones (Zephras Isle, Riverglades, Shen'dralas, Mount Hyjal), adds Dalaran in the Alterac Mountains, and expands the Wetlands, Desolace and Azshara.

statements.title: Zone level ranges and new zones (scope: forever)
statements.text: Level ranges for Classic zones in Forever are essentially the same as in Classic. A table based on patch 1.60.1 matches the Classic table almost exactly.

statements.title: Zone level ranges and new zones (scope: forever)
statements.text: Riverglades is a contested zone in south-east Khaz Modan, east of the Badlands and Burning Steppes. Hubs: Farholde Keep (Alliance flight path), Rog'mar (Horde flight path), Bolder'ok (ogres allied with the Horde), Powderfuse Port (neutral, boat to Tanaris).

statements.title: Zone level ranges and new zones (scope: forever)
statements.text: Riverglades range: 35–45 (wiki), 36–44 (Wowhead Forever database, second-hand; also two zone tables), or 33–54 (group finder). Polestar routes it at 41–45 (Alliance) and 41–44 (Horde).

statements.title: Zone level ranges and new zones (scope: forever)
statements.text: Riverglades has more than 150 quests. A later figure is "nearly 200".

statements.title: Zone level ranges and new zones (scope: forever)
statements.text: Riverglades access: on foot from Redridge (Redridge Pass or Blackrock Pass), the Badlands, Swamp of Sorrows or Burning Steppes, or by boat from Tanaris. Flights: Alliance from Lakeshire, Morgan's Vigil or Thelsamar; Horde from Stonard, Kargath, Flame Crest or Hammerfall.

statements.title: Zone level ranges and new zones (scope: forever)
statements.text: Riverglades mobs were over-tuned at launch and toned down on Nov 11 (for example, one Twilight Forgemaster ability went from 1,000 to 50 bonus damage).

statements.title: Zone level ranges and new zones (scope: forever)
statements.text: Shen'dralas is a contested zone in central Kalimdor, reached on foot from Desolace through the Valley of Bones. It has no flight master. Its quests run about 38–45 and open at 35.

statements.title: Zone level ranges and new zones (scope: forever)
statements.text: The Shen'dralas level range is the least settled of any zone: 40–45, 45–53, 35–45 or "30–50". Polestar routes it at 45–47.

statements.title: Zone level ranges and new zones (scope: forever)
statements.text: Mount Hyjal is a level-60 contested zone, reached on foot from Winterspring. It holds the raids Barrow Deeps (10-player) and Hyjal Summit (20-player), which open 2026-12-09. Other ranges given: 54–60 and 55–60.

statements.title: Zone level ranges and new zones (scope: forever)
statements.text: Two sites say Feralas and Felwood open earlier than in Classic (35 and 45). Other tables keep the Classic ranges.

statements.title: Group vs solo (scope: forever)
statements.text: Group with players in your own level range to keep kill XP steady. Higher-level members reduce your XP.

statements.title: Group vs solo (scope: forever)
statements.text: In dungeons, a member more than 12 levels above an enemy cancels its kill XP for everyone.

statements.title: Group vs solo (scope: forever)
statements.text: The first Forever level-60 characters were a group of five (three mages, a paladin and a shaman). They reached 60 about 52 hours after launch, levelling together with large open-world area-of-effect pulls and keeping their levels in step.

statements.title: Group vs solo (scope: forever)
statements.text: Several hotfixes made quest drops shared with every eligible party member (e.g. Deadwood Key, Blackthorne Intelligence, Shen'dralas pylon repairs), which makes questing in a group smoother.

statements.title: Group vs solo (scope: forever)
statements.text: Classes that heal themselves or kite fare best alone, and that saves hours of levelling.

statements.title: Group vs solo (scope: forever)
statements.text: Players asked for shared mob tagging; the team reportedly ruled it out in an interview. The primary source was not checked.

statements.title: Group vs solo (scope: forever)
statements.text: One shop-run site estimates that Mages and Hunters level about 8% faster than average and Warriors about 12% slower.

statements.title: Mount timing, gold and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: The first mount comes at level 40. Apprentice Riding costs 100 g and includes a basic racial mount (+60% speed). Extra colours cost 20 g. These figures are from the beta.

statements.title: Mount timing, gold and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: At 60, Journeyman Riding costs 1,000 g plus 200 g for an epic mount (+100% speed). Honored reputation gives 10% off. The Legacy talent Bartering gives up to 10% more off mounts, but not off the riding skill or class training.

statements.title: Mount timing, gold and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: Warlocks: the Summon Felsteed quest now grants Apprentice Riding, and characters who finished it earlier get the skill on their first summon.

statements.title: Mount timing, gold and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: At level 40, Alliance Paladins get their mount through The Tome of Nobility. For Forsaken Paladins, the quest is A Paladin’s Steed, which starts and ends with Danitha Morr.

statements.title: Mount timing, gold and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: Since a hotfix, racial mounts bought from a vendor bind to the buyer (BoP).

statements.title: Mount timing, gold and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: Training every class ability from 1 to 60 costs about 206–207 g for every class. Warlock costs were lowered to make room for buying pet Grimoires.

statements.title: Mount timing, gold and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: Dual Specialization unlocks at level 40. Price: 50 g according to the wiki and Method; kami-labs says it was never announced.

statements.title: Mount timing, gold and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: On the beta a respec cost 1 silver if you had not respecced recently, rose with each reset and fell back after an hour. Live pricing is unconfirmed.

statements.title: Mount timing, gold and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: Ways to save gold: loot everything, avoid unnecessary purchases, put off expensive buys until 60, and check what unknown items are worth before selling them to a vendor.

statements.title: Mount timing, gold and training cost (scope: forever)
statements.text: Keep your main damage or healing spell at its newest rank when you train. The addons "What's Training? (Forever)" and "ForeverTrainer" help decide what to buy.

statements.title: Death avoidance (scope: forever)
statements.text: Below level 10, releasing at the spirit healer costs nothing. From 10 onwards it costs durability and gives a 10-minute debuff, so run back to your corpse. Classic starts resurrection sickness at 11; Forever's threshold is not confirmed officially.

statements.title: Death avoidance (scope: forever)
statements.text: Repair often: broken weapons deal no damage and broken armour gives no protection.

statements.title: Death avoidance (scope: forever)
statements.text: Pull one mob at a time from range, pull casters by breaking line of sight, and crowd-control humanoids that flee.

statements.title: Death avoidance (scope: forever)
statements.text: Polestar keeps solo players off mobs 2 or more levels above them and warns at +1. Version 0.4.0 cut such spots from about 106 to 58 (Alliance) and from 102 to 47 (Horde).

statements.title: Death avoidance (scope: forever)
statements.text: Known launch hazards, since fixed: over-tuned Riverglades mobs (fixed Nov 11), a 30% damage bug in The Drowned City (fixed Nov 9), and Young Diemetradons in Un'Goro spawning at level 58 instead of 51–52 (fixed Nov 9).

statements.title: Death avoidance (scope: forever)
statements.text: The spirit-healer penalty from level 10 makes deliberately dying to travel back to town costlier than in Classic. This is an inference from #1.

statements.title: Death avoidance (scope: forever)
statements.text: Hardcore mode is not live at launch.

statements.title: Hardcore-derived survival habits (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Fight mobs at your level or green mobs. Higher-level mobs lower your hit chance.

statements.title: Hardcore-derived survival habits (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Stay on roads and don't run through packs: getting dazed with several mobs chasing you is a common death.

statements.title: Pace, time-to-60 and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: Developers reportedly said the average time to level 20 is 20.5 hours in Forever versus 20.4 hours in Classic. This was seen only via a search snippet; the original podcast was not checked. No official 1–60 time exists.

statements.title: Pace, time-to-60 and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: Polestar's simulated 1–60 /played, including rested XP, is about 127.5 h for Alliance and 120.9 h for Horde. The authors call these estimates and say the guide is not built for speed-levelling. Each simulated run includes about 30 hours of grinding.

statements.title: Pace, time-to-60 and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: Third-party estimates for 1–60 range from 50 to 200 hours, for example about 150 h (LFCarry) and 100–120 h for a first character.

statements.title: Pace, time-to-60 and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: The first Forever level-60s took about 52 hours of real time with a coordinated group of five.

statements.title: Pace, time-to-60 and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: Session routine: plan each session around a hub, finish in an inn and bind the hearthstone to the next session's starting hub (see KB-G04 #11).

statements.title: Pace, time-to-60 and session planning (scope: forever)
statements.text: Classic reference points: the 2019 world-first took 3 days 7 hours /played, and the fastest reported Classic /played is about 21 hours (classic_fallback).

statements.title: Professions while levelling (scope: forever)
statements.text: Two gathering professions (Herbalism, Mining, Skinning) give the most gold for the least investment while levelling. Avoid two crafting professions with no gatherer.

statements.title: Professions while levelling (scope: forever)
statements.text: Learn Cooking early: a Basic Campfire needs only Cooking 1, and cooked food gives +5% kill XP.

statements.title: Professions while levelling (scope: forever)
statements.text: Profession camp features unlock at skill 20, so get professions to 20 early. Leatherworking's Camp Tent gives rested XP; Alchemy's Mana Well helps mana regeneration.

statements.title: Professions while levelling (scope: forever)
statements.text: First Aid is buffed in Forever, with more craftable items than just bandages. In Classic the advice was to get First Aid to about 150 early.

statements.title: Professions while levelling (scope: forever)
statements.text: Enchanting and Tailoring give access to early wands (Lesser and Greater Magic Wand), which matter for Priests, Mages and Warlocks. At launch you may have to craft one yourself.

statements.title: Professions while levelling (scope: forever)
statements.text: Profession Legacy points come at skill 150, 225 and 300. Reaching 150 in a non-gathering profession can unlock the Legacy system.

statements.title: Professions while levelling (scope: forever)
statements.text: Mages have a new minor tradeskill, Comprehension: "Comprehend Scroll" reads scrolls that drop from creatures and gives buffs.

statements.title: Legacy system, levelling-relevant (scope: forever)
statements.text: The Legacy system is account-wide. It unlocks with your first Legacy point, normally when your first character reaches 25, or at 150 in a non-gathering profession, or after exploring the whole world map.

statements.title: Legacy system, levelling-relevant (scope: forever)
statements.text: There are 65 challenges, each worth one point. Class challenges: reaching 25, 45 and 60 on each of the nine classes (27 points). Tradeskill challenges: 18. PvP: 12. Adventure: 2. Dungeons: 3 (final bosses of all dungeons in the 15–25, 26–45 and 46–60 brackets). Raids: 3.

statements.title: Legacy system, levelling-relevant (scope: forever)
statements.text: At launch each character can spend up to 16 points across the Professions, Adventure and Resourcefulness trees.

statements.title: Legacy system, levelling-relevant (scope: forever)
statements.text: Adventure perks for levelling: "Talented" unlocks talent points up to 5 levels early, and "Frequent Flier" makes flights cheaper and faster.

statements.title: Legacy system, levelling-relevant (scope: forever)
statements.text: "Well Rested" gives up to +20% rested build-up rate and cap (guide figures).

statements.title: Legacy system, levelling-relevant (scope: forever)
statements.text: "Reagent Economy" removes vendor reagents for class abilities (fixed on Nov 17).

statements.title: Legacy system, levelling-relevant (scope: forever)
statements.text: Blizzard fixed a bug with The Quick and the Dead on Nov 6 without naming the affected spells. A separate beta fix removed Bartering discounts on training and repairs.

statements.title: Legacy system, levelling-relevant (scope: forever)
statements.text: Talent orders tied to levels shift by up to 5 levels for players with "Talented". Beta builds assume 5 points in it.

statements.title: Legacy system, levelling-relevant (scope: forever)
statements.text: Contradiction: the wiki lists the class point levels as 25, 40 and 60; Blizzard says 25, 45 and 60. Use Blizzard's.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Talents start at level 10, one point per level, for 51 points at 60.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Each tree has gold-medal milestone talents at 11, 16 (new), 21 and 31 points.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Respecs, including Legacy talents, are done at a class trainer in a major city. Dual Specialization unlocks at 40.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Trees keep Classic's overall shape and row count, but many talents were changed, removed, made baseline or replaced. Classic point-by-point orders do not apply to Forever.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Hit and crit are each a single stat across spells, melee and ranged.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Caster weapons now carry spell damage and healing.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Newly learned spells are no longer placed on action bars automatically, so the coach should remind players to drag them on after training.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Most talents no longer reduce their proc chance when you cast low-rank spells. A reduced chance still applies to ranks learned more than 12 levels below your level; Arcane Concentration, Frostbite and Fingers of Frost are named as keeping this rule.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Wands and Auto Shot need you to stand still for 0.5 seconds before firing. Scrolls are on the global cooldown.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: The weapon-skill system remains but is less generous. Items give much less skill (e.g. Edgemaster's Handguards +1 instead of +7). Racial weapon-skill bonuses were removed or converted to crit (Human Sword and Orc Axe now give crit). Dwarf Mace Specialization became Earth Fury (+2% crit damage and healing).

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: New weapon skills start at 1 and are bought from trainers, so level them on weak enemies first.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Racial changes at launch: Human Spirit +10%; Tauren Plainsrunning up to 60% speed; Orc Blood Fury cooldown 2 minutes; Troll Berserking 15 seconds; Skyborne Skysight +15% speed.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Class/race availability: Paladin is Human, Dwarf or Undead (Undead is new and the only Horde option). Shaman is Orc, Tauren, Troll, Skyborne or Dwarf (Dwarf is new and the only Alliance option). Druid is Night Elf, Tauren or Skyborne.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: Blessing of Salvation in all its forms was removed, and Bear Form threat was raised to compensate.

statements.title: Talent system and Forever-wide class rules (scope: forever)
statements.text: One community site says bonus healing also gives one third of its value as bonus damage for hybrid classes. Snippet only; not in official notes.

statements.title: Premise check, "class weapon grants" (scope: forever)
statements.text: The only Blizzard wording found: because caster weapons now carry spell power, casters can look forward to "level-up weapons" the way Warriors, Rogues and Hunters already do. In context this means ordinary weapon upgrades while levelling, not a system that hands out weapons.

statements.title: Premise check, "class weapon grants" (scope: forever)
statements.text: No patch note, hotfix or guide describes weapons being given automatically on level-up.

statements.title: Premise check, "class weapon grants" (scope: forever)
statements.text: Class weapon *quests* do exist: Warrior Whirlwind weapons (30); Rogue Ruby-Adorned Blade (starts 23, plan for about 30); Shaman Rage of the Storm (30, after Call of Air); Mage (30); Paladin Verigan's Fist or Wolfsbane (20). Hunter, Druid and Priest have no weapon quest before 60.

statements.title: Premise check, "class weapon grants" (scope: forever)
statements.text: Warcraft Tavern says wands and weapons received major stat boosts in Forever, without numbers.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Victory Rush is a new baseline ability at 20. After a kill that gives XP or honour it heals about 10% of maximum health, with a 30-second cooldown.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Tactical Mastery is baseline at 14 and keeps 10 rage when you change stance. Improved Tactical Mastery is a 3-point talent (5/10/15 rage).

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Rage from damage dealt is normalised to weapon speed, and critical hits give 75% more rage. Warcraft Tavern says rage generation is much lower than in Classic and decays out of combat.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Slam has a 1.5-second cast and a 15-second cooldown; Improved Slam lowers the cooldown by 2.5 or 5 seconds. Thunder Clap can be used in Defensive Stance and also slows attack speed by 20%. Defensive Stance threat is +80%. Berserker Rage comes at 30.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: The weapon specialisations were merged into Weaponmaster. Other new talents include Spearing Strike, Bloodthrill (Rend and white hits can enable Overpower; 2 points), Vanguard (Charge in Defensive Stance), Bastion, Boundless Rage, Reckless Swings and Improved Whirlwind.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Launch talent changes: Two-Handed Weapon Specialization 2/4/6%; Defiance 7/13/20%; Fury tree reworked (Flurry no longer needs Death Wish, Bloodthirst does). Flurry is 3 points (10/20/30%).

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Rend scales with attack power and its ticks can crit, which makes Improved Rend a strong early pick.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spells: Ability levels: Battle Shout and Heroic Strike 1; Rend and Charge 4; Thunder Clap 6; Hamstring 8; Bloodrage and the stance quests 10; Overpower 12; Revenge and Demoralizing Shout 14; Victory Rush, Cleave, Slam, Retaliation, Polearms and Dual Wield 20; Execute 24; Berserker Stance and Intercept (quest) 30; Whirlwind 36; Plate 40. These come from one guide's table; Slam at 20 and Execute at 24 are unconfirmed elsewhere.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Method (updated Nov 14) recommends Protection with one-hand and shield for solo levelling and grinding, and Arms with a two-hander for groups.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Method's Arms order: Improved Rend → Tactical Mastery / Deep Wounds → Bloodthrill, Sweeping Strikes, Weaponmaster → Mortal Strike → Unbridled Wrath / Enrage.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Method's Protection order: Shield Specialization → Improved Thunder Clap / Improved Bloodrage → (20) Master of Defense, Improved Revenge, Vanguard → Bastion / Focused Rage.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Warcraft Tavern (beta, level-30 builds) treats Arms as the traditional pick and Protection as strong too; Fury is weak before 30. Its Arms build predates the Nov 2 changes.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Rotation: Before talents: Battle Shout, Charge, Rend, Heroic Strike. Use Hamstring to kite and Thunder Clap on several mobs.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Stats: Weapon damage > Strength/attack power > Stamina > Agility > Armour. Weapons provide about 95–100% of a levelling warrior's damage.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Weapons: Prefer slow, heavy weapons: they boost instant attacks. Under normalised rage a slow weapon no longer gives more rage per swing. Warriors start in mail and train plate at 40. They can use every weapon type except wands.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Weapons: Two-handed options for levels 1–30: Forsaken Greataxe (15, Horde), Ironforge Greathammer (16, Alliance, Hall of Thanes), Axe of Orgrimmar (16, Horde, RFC), Smite's Mighty Hammer (18, Deadmines), Heavehammer (24, Wetlands), Corpsemaker (29, RFK), Manual Crowd Pummeler (29, Gnomeregan).

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Quests: Level 10: race-specific quests teach Defensive Stance, Taunt and Sunder Armor. Level 20: the Brutal Hauberk / Fire Hardened Hauberk quest. Level 30: The Affray (Berserker Stance and Intercept).

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Quests: Whirlwind weapon chain at 30 (The Islander → The Affray → The Summoning, ending with a level-40 elite). Reward: Whirlwind Axe, Sword or Warhammer (item level 40), each given +1 Strength and +1 Stamina in Forever. The chain is hard at 30: buy the reagents or bring help.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Quests: "Thur'Grim's Axe" is listed as a level-10 class reward by a single source only.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Mistakes: Wasting rage on overkill Executes, losing rage to unplanned stance swaps, sitting on cooldowns, using fast weapons, and switching to a new weapon type without training its skill.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: forever)
statements.text: Solo/group: The hardest solo class of the three melee classes: punishing against higher-level mobs and little self-healing beyond Victory Rush. Group with a healer, and use dungeons to get the weapons that let you outscale mobs.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic advice values 1 weapon DPS at about 7 Strength.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Skip Mocking Blow and most Protection abilities, and keep rank 1 of Thunder Clap, Cleave and Shield Bash. **✗** for Thunder Clap: Forever adds a slow and Protection talents to it.

statements.title: Warrior (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Carry plenty of food and bandages, and use a swing-timer addon.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Shank is a new baseline ability at 24 (rank 2 at 44). It costs 5 energy, has a 10-second cooldown, strikes with the off-hand for 50% weapon damage, cannot miss and generates 15 energy (25 at rank 2).

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Poised (18): at full energy out of combat, your next energy ability costs 10 less.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: The attack-power scaling of poisons was doubled. Poisons have more charges, can crit, and stack with sharpening stones and Windfury. Sap no longer breaks stealth.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Rogues can use one-handed axes. Default weapon skills are daggers, axes and thrown weapons.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Talent rework. Assassination gains Mutilate, Venom, Blood Splatter and Composure. Combat gains Flash of Steel, Coup de Grace, Efficient Strikes and Hack and Slash (which works with any weapon type and replaces the weapon specialisations). Subtlety gains Death Mark, Boot Knife, Quick Getaway, and a Ghostly Strike that allows Ambush and Garrote in combat. Removed: Murder, Quietus, Cutthroat, Thousand Cuts, Improved Distract.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Method: Combat for solo, Subtlety in groups, Assassination viable. Consider Subtlety from about 30 if you have a strong dagger. Combat takes Blade Flurry early, dips into Assassination for Cold Blood and prioritises Riposte.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Warcraft Tavern offers four builds: Assassination, Combat, Subtlety Ambush and Subtlety Bleed. Subtlety Bleed is weak until Blood Splatter, after 50.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Rotation: Apply poisons, then open with Garrote if the mob will live through it, otherwise Ambush. Use Shank on cooldown, build with Sinister Strike, Backstab or Mutilate, keep Slice and Dice up, and finish with Eviscerate. Use Expose Armor only on long fights.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spells: Key levels: Dual Wield and Slice and Dice 10; Kick 12; Ambush and Poised 18; Vanish 22; Shank 24; Cheap Shot 26; Kidney Shot and Blade Flurry 30.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Stats: Early: Agility > attack power > Strength > Stamina > Armour. Later: Crit > Agility > attack power > Strength > Stamina. Weapon upgrades give the largest gains.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Weapons: Combat should avoid daggers, because Sinister Strike hits harder with other weapons; put the highest-DPS weapon in the main hand. Assassination and Subtlety prefer daggers. Replace the starter weapon as soon as possible.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Weapons: Good drops: Cruel Barb (Deadmines), Meteor Shard and Butcher's Slicer (SFK), Outlaw Sabre (BFD quest), Meathook Slicer (Ruins of Lordaeron).

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Quests: The poisons class quest is at 20. Alliance: Mathias and the Defias, Klaven's Tower, The Touch of Zanzil. Horde: The Shattered Salute, Deep Cover, Mission: Possible But Not Possible, Hinott's Assistance. The faction split comes from a badly parsed table and should be verified.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Quests: The Ruby-Adorned Blade chain (one-handed sword, item level 36) is new in Forever. It starts at 23 with The Horn of Xelthos, includes Shadowfang Keep and ends with a solo heist in Scarlet Monastery. Plan for about 30.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Quests: "Blade of Cunning" (a level-10 dagger) is listed by a single source.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Poisons: Use Deadly and Instant Poison once both are available (about 30). The others are mostly for PvP.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Mistakes: Opening every mob from stealth early on (stealth slows you), switching targets with unspent combo points, careless stuns and incapacitates, and letting Remorseless Attacks lapse.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: forever)
statements.text: Solo/group: Solo as Combat. In groups play Subtlety, use Feint to shed threat and Backstab from behind.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: **✗** Slice and Dice is only worth using from 42. Forever guides use it from 10.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: **✗** Classic Combat Swords / Dagger Specialization talent orders no longer apply: Hack and Slash replaced the weapon specialisations.

statements.title: Rogue (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Solo rogues rarely get behind mobs, so Backstab is unreliable when solo. Run dungeons every few levels for weapons, and use Sap, Gouge and Blind to keep fights one-on-one.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Launch buffs: Aimed Shot bonus damage about +110%, Arcane Shot about +30% (attack-power coefficient 0.15), Serpent Sting about +20%. Aspect of the Hawk gives 20/35/50/70/90/110 ranged attack power by rank. All traps share a 30-second cooldown. Hunter's Mark ranks no longer stack. Lightning Reflexes gives 3–15% Agility. Orc Command returned (+5% pet damage).

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Auto Shot needs you to stand still for 0.5 seconds.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Aimed Shot is available at 20 as a baseline ability.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Survival was reworked towards melee: Mongoose Bite and Immolation Trap at 16, Strider Kick and Expose Prey at 30, plus Lacerating Strikes. Marksmanship gets Lone Wolf, Sniper Shot (40) and Trueshot Aura (25). Scorpid Sting now lowers the target's hit chance by 2%.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: New or updated pet family abilities, including Fox (Trickster's Dance), Bear Swipe, Bat Sonic Blast, Croc Dismember, Hyena Tendon Rip, Raptor Savage Rend and Spider Web.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Pet damage in PvE is normalised by the family's attack speed. Pets receive camping buffs. Untrained pets keep their natural attack-speed passives.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Beast Mastery is the consensus levelling spec.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Method's order: 10–24 Deadly Aspects → Focused Fire → Improved Revive Pet → 1 point in Endurance Training → Pathfinding (20) / Unleashed Fury. 25–40 Summon Hawk → Bestial Swiftness → Intimidation → Bestial Wrath (Unleashed Fury and Frenzy 4/5, Bestial Discipline). 41–60: 20 points in Marksmanship (Lethal Attacks, Careful Aim, Rapid Killing, Efficiency, Trueshot Aura, Mortal Shots 4/5).

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Summon Hawk (talent, 25) summons hawks that last 18 seconds, up to two at once, sharing a 6-second cooldown with Arcane Shot. Recast only at the last moment. After Summon Hawk, Arcane Shot is mostly redundant for Beast Mastery.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Warcraft Tavern: aim Beast Mastery at Bestial Wrath, prioritising Pathfinding and Efficiency. Marksmanship is less forgiving and Survival demanding. Avoid Lone Wolf while levelling.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Stats: Beast Mastery and Marksmanship: Agility > attack power > Crit > Intellect > Spirit > Stamina > Strength. Survival values Strength more.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Weapons: Bow or gun: the Dwarf gun and Troll bow racial bonuses are gone, so use whichever ranged weapon has the highest DPS (inference from S43).

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Weapons: Ranged weapons for levels 1–30: Misplaced Shooter (10, Horde), Harvester's Pestslayer (13, Alliance), Barbaric Crossbow (13, Horde, RFC), Calibrated Blunderbuss (16, Alliance, Hall of Thanes), Venomstrike (19, WC), Naga Heartpiercer / Fallenroot Longbow (22–23, BFD), Gravespike Repeater (26), Golemsight Long Gun (28), Master Hunter's Bow and Quilboar Blaster (30).

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Pets: Cat is the top levelling pet (fast, high DPS). Boar is the sturdy alternative and has Charge. Boars and bears eat almost anything, so they are easy to feed. One source prefers a bear for Beast Mastery.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Pets: The first pet at 10 comes with Growl, Great Stamina and Natural Armor. Mend Pet at 12. Dash is learned by taming a beast that has it.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Quests: "Taming the Beast" chain at 10, including in the Zephras Isle start. There is no hunter weapon quest before 60.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Mistakes: Pulling before the pet has threat, pulling several mobs, running so low on mana there is none left for Feign Death, using Aspect of the Cheetah or Pack in combat, neglecting pet food, Mend Pet and pet training, recasting Hawk too early, and relying on Feign Death (it can be resisted).

statements.title: Hunter (scope: forever)
statements.text: Solo/group: The strongest solo class of the three physical classes. In groups, turn off Growl and avoid extra pulls.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Stat order: Agility > Intellect > Spirit > Stamina > Strength.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Skippable: Eagle Eye, Eyes of the Beast, Scare Beast, Mongoose Bite, most Tracking, Scorpid Sting, Flare, Viper Sting, Volley, Explosive Trap, Aspect of the Wild. **✗ partly**: Mongoose Bite matters for Forever Survival, and Scorpid Sting was reworked.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Rank 1 Wing Clip is enough, and higher ranks of Arcane Shot and Multi-Shot can be skipped. **✗** for Arcane Shot before Summon Hawk, because Forever buffed it.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Ammo upgrade points: 1, 10, 25, 40 and 52.

statements.title: Hunter (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: **✗** Classic Beast Mastery orders (Improved Aspect of the Hawk, Thick Hide, etc.) do not match Forever's talents (Deadly Aspects, Focused Fire, Summon Hawk, Lone Wolf).

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Cone of Cold lasts less time, explicitly to curb mass kiting. Improved Blizzard's slow is capped at 40% (Classic: 65%). Permafrost now extends Chill by 11/22/33%. Cold Snap is a 21-point talent with a 10-minute cooldown.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Frostfire Bolt is learned at 40: a 3-second cast with a damage-over-time effect and a slow, using your better spell power against the target's lower resistance.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Ice Lance is a Frost talent: instant, +300% damage against frozen targets, sharing an 8-second cooldown with Fire Blast. Fingers of Frost makes targets count as frozen.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Launch changes: Elemental Precision became Precision (3 points, 2/4/6% hit with all spells, with Arcane Focus merged in). Piercing Ice and the Frost Blast spell were removed. Ice Barrier gives +15% Frost damage for a minute. Winter's Chill adds 20% per stack to Cone of Cold. Improved Fireball is renamed Accelerant. Critical Mass is 3 points again.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Arcane: Arcane Blast and Missile Barrage are talents, Arcane Wrath is a new 16-point talent, and Wand Specialization costs 2 points. Arcane Blast stacks last 18 seconds and each stack adds 100% to its mana cost.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Comprehension is a new minor tradeskill: "Comprehend Scroll" reads scrolls that drop from creatures and gives buffs. One guide says it is learned at 6. The Research spell was removed and only "Study" remains after the relevant quest.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Mage Armor gives more regeneration based on Spirit; one guide says it is learned at 34.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Frost is the consensus solo spec.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Method's order: 10–25 Improved Frostbolt, Precision, Frostbite, Ice Lance, 3 points in Ice Shards, Ice Block at 25. 26–42 Shatter, Fingers of Frost, Improved Cone of Cold, Winter's Chill, Cold Snap, Ice Barrier, then finish Improved Cone of Cold and Ice Shards. 43–60 Arcane: Improved Channeling 5, Arcane Concentration, Missile Barrage, Arcane Subtlety, Arcane Blast (57), Arcane Meditation. Optional: 2 points in Wand Specialization at 12–13.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Frost. The levelling build ends near 12/0/39; key talents and the level to have them by: Improved Frostbolt 5 by 16; Ice Lance by 20; Ice Block by 27; Cold Snap by 33; Ice Barrier by 40.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Warcraft Tavern's Frost build instead opens with 7 Arcane points for early Missile Barrage. It also offers Arcane and Fire builds. Its builds were capped at 30.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spells: Polymorph at 8. Level 20 brings Blizzard, Ice Lance (talent), Blink and teleports. Frostfire Bolt at 40.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spells: Rank-1 Frostbolt is useful for cheap kiting or fishing for Missile Barrage procs. With Permafrost, use max rank for the longest slow. Proc talents lose chance on ranks more than 12 levels below you, so rank-1 fishing fades as you level.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Stats: Early: Intellect / spell damage > Stamina / Spirit > Armour. Fire and Frost: spell damage > Intellect > mana per 5 > Stamina > Spirit. Arcane: Intellect > spell damage > Spirit > mana per 5.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Weapons: Gear path: Novice's Practice Wand (1), Greater Magic Wand (13), Coldspire Staff (19), Gravestone Scepter (27), Icefury Wand (30, best at 40), Orb of the Forgotten Seer (32), Hypnotic Blade (34).

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Quests: Class quests at 10, 15 and 26: the Classic robe and Mirror Lake chains plus Forever additions such as the Alliance-only "Mage-tastic Gizmonitor". One guide says Horde mages can train in Dalaran with Jessa Weaver, but this "may change".

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Mistakes: Overusing Arcane Blast, expecting Classic-style mass kiting, pulling packs that include ranged mobs, and forgetting to put new ranks on the action bars.

statements.title: Mage (scope: forever)
statements.text: Solo/group: Kiting small groups in the open world still works. Classic-style dungeon area-of-effect farming is what the nerfs target. Blizzard is still strong if mobs stay inside it and nothing hits you while you channel.

statements.title: Mage (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: **✗** Classic Frost levelling (Frostbite 3, Shatter 5, Ice Shards 5, or an Improved Arcane Missiles opener) does not transfer: Shatter, Winter's Chill and Permafrost were rescaled.

statements.title: Mage (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Rank skips for single-target Frost: skip Dampen Magic, Amplify Magic, Slow Fall, Detect Magic and Flamestrike ranks; rank 1 of Fireball and Blizzard is enough. Re-check against Forever's flat ~206 g training cost.

statements.title: Mage (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Stats: spell or Frost damage > Intellect > Stamina > Spirit. A one-hander plus off-hand usually beats a staff. Get a wand early.

statements.title: Mage (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Don't take Frostbite in an area-of-effect build, because random freezes break the kite.

statements.title: Mage (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: The Icefury Wand quest chain (30) is hardest at its Scarlet Monastery Library step.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Curse of Agony and Curse of Doom became "Banes", so a target can carry one Bane and one Curse. Curse of Shadows was removed. Curse of the Elements now covers every magic school.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Life Tap scales with Spirit.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Drain Soul's chance to give a soul shard on damage ticks was heavily reduced at launch, so finish mobs with Drain Soul.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Pets scale from the warlock's stats. At launch pet health per point of the warlock's Stamina fell from 7.5 to 2. The Voidwalker got about 40 extra base health on Nov 6.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: 17 talents were removed, including Improved Drain Life, Dark Pact, Fel Intellect, Fel Stamina, Improved Firebolt, Improved Lash of Pain, Devastation and Improved Immolate. Grim Reach was removed and then re-added on Oct 15 as a range talent (+10/20%).
Wrack's damage was cut by 30% on 10 Nov (confirmed in Blizzard's hotfix list), and it now speeds up Corruption, Siphon Life and Bane of Agony ticks instead of raising their damage.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Firestone and Spellstone are weapon imbues that stack with wizard oils; Spellstone boosts Shadow only. Meeting stones no longer summon, so Ritual of Summoning is the only summon. Fear has a 20-yard range.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Affliction is the consensus levelling spec. Every source opens with Improved Corruption 5 and takes Suppression early.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Affliction. The levelling build ends near 45/6/0; key talents and the level to have them by: Improved Corruption 5 by 18; Fel Concentration 3 by 25; Siphon Life by 36; Amplify Curse by 38; Wrack by 50.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Affliction variants. Some builds take Demonic Embrace 5, Demonic Aegis 2, Fel Vitality 2 in place of Unholy Power, Soul Harvest, Amplify Curse; others Improved Shadow Bolt 5, Bane 5, Curse of Exhaustion 1 in place of Unholy Power, Malevolence, Improved Life Tap; others Bane 5, Cataclysm 3 in place of Unholy Power, Grim Reach, Fel Vitality.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Pets: Imp at 1. Voidwalker at 10 (Horde: the Undercity version is easier). Succubus or Incubus at 20 (the Horde chain is 8 quests across the Barrens and Stonetalon). Felhunter at 30 ("Seeking Strahad"). Felsteed at 40, Dreadsteed at 60.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Pets: Use the Voidwalker from about 10 to 20, and the Succubus for drain-tanking from about 30. Buy every rank of Torment. Because of the launch cut to pet health, expect the Voidwalker to tank worse than beta guides suggest. Demon trainers sell Grimoires; Blood Pact is available at 4.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spells: Key levels: 1 Shadow Bolt, Demon Skin, Immolate. 4 Corruption, Curse of Weakness. 6 Life Tap. 8 Bane of Agony. 10 Drain Soul, Healthstone. 14 Drain Life. 18 Soulstone, Searing Pain. 20 Demon Armor, Rain of Fire, Ritual of Summoning. 24 Shadowburn. 30 Siphon Life. One guide puts Create Firestone at 28 and Create Spellstone at 36.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spells: Wait until about 37 for Siphon Life, because rank 1 is weak. Don't use Searing Pain before Demonic Brand, as it pulls aggro off the pet. Bane of Doom is for bosses only.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Stats: Affliction and Demonology: spell power > wand DPS (until 30) > Spirit/Intellect > Stamina. Spirit is worth more than in Classic because Life Tap scales with it.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Weapons: Wands: Lesser and Greater Magic Wand (Enchanting), Gravestone Scepter (BFD quest "Blackfathom Villainy"), Dancing Flame (26, Horde), White Obsidian (39), Peacekeeper (43), Wand of Biting Cold (51). Staves are preferred because off-hands are scarce; Staff of the Shade (RFK) is good from 22. Staff/Orb of Soran'ruk come from a level-20 quest.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Rotation: Bane of Agony → Corruption → Immolate, then wand (before about 30) or Drain Life. Life Tap when health is well above mana, Drain Life when mana is well above health. Keep 2–3 spare shards.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Mistakes: Wanding at full mana, Drain Life at full health, DoTs on dying mobs, Shadow Bolt on a feared target, Searing Pain before Demonic Brand, letting Demon Skin/Armor drop, expecting shards from Drain Soul damage ticks, and following Classic builds.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: forever)
statements.text: Solo/group: Strong solo through drain-tanking. Destruction suits dungeons. Ritual of Summoning makes warlocks valuable to groups.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: **✗** Classic builds using Improved Drain Life, Dark Pact, Fel Stamina or Fel Intellect are invalid: those talents were removed.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Rank-1 only: Drain Soul, Curse of Recklessness, Howl of Terror, Banish. Skip until 60: Curse of Weakness, Drain Mana, Curse of the Elements, Firestone, Detect Invisibility, Subjugate Demon, Hellfire, Rain of Fire, Soul Fire. **✗ partly**: Forever changed Curse of the Elements (every school), Firestone (now an imbue) and Drain Soul (shards).

statements.title: Warlock (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: **✗** Classic ranks Stamina high, because Life Tap converted health. Forever's Spirit-based Life Tap and the cut to pet health make Stamina relatively less valuable.

statements.title: Warlock (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Classic sources disagree on Succubus vs Felhunter as the main pet.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Every race gets Fear Ward and Devouring Plague at 20, Divine Spirit at 30 and Shadow Word: Death at 32.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Shadow Word: Death costs 30% of your maximum health if the target survives (nothing on a miss), with an 18-second cooldown. Treat it strictly as an execute. Devouring Plague has a 24-second cooldown.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Racial spells were reworked and are learned through class quests at 10 and 20. Gnome (new): Confounding Flash, Contingency Plan. Human: Divine Grace, Feedback. Dwarf: Desperate Prayer, Chastise. Night Elf: Starshards, Elune's Grace. Undead: Touch of Weakness, Dark Sacrifice. Troll: unchanged.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Wand Specialization costs 2 points. Meditation's regeneration was raised substantially. Penance is a 21-point talent. Shadowform (31 points) allows all non-healing spells, halves Shadow mana costs and doubles the Shadow crit bonus. Vampiric Embrace is a 16-point talent. Shadow Focus gives hit.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Fade's threat reduction is doubled. Cure Disease, Abolish Disease, Fear Ward and Confounding Flash no longer break Shadowform.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Binding Heal: the official notes say it was removed, while kami-labs' datamine shows a trainer spell from 25. Unresolved.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: The official deep dive does not mention Spirit Tap, so whether it exists in Forever is unconfirmed.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Method: a mana-efficient, sturdy build leaning Discipline for levels 1–39, then respec to Shadow at 40 for Shadowform. The exact talent picks were in images that could not be read.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Warcraft Tavern (beta): a Discipline wand build (Inner Focus 20, Penance 30, Power Infusion 40), or Shadow (Mind Flay 20, Vampiric Embrace 25, Silence 30, Shadowform 40). Shadow is weak before about 28 without spell power. Holy is not recommended for levelling.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spells: Key levels: Shadow Word: Pain 4; Power Word: Shield 6; Mind Blast 10; Inner Fire 12; Psychic Scream 14; Devouring Plague and Fear Ward 20; Shadow Word: Death 32; Shadowform and Mind Flay rank 3 at 40; Prayer of Fortitude 48. Method advises against buying every rank on a fresh server, but names no specific ranks to skip.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Rotation: 1–9: Smite and Shadow Word: Pain. 10–39: Shield, Mind Blast, Shadow Word: Pain, then wand. 40+ Shadow: Mind Blast and Shadow Word: Death (execute only) on cooldown, Mind Flay as filler. Open with Shadow Word: Pain to win tags.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Stats: Intellect / spell damage (Shadow power for Shadow) > Stamina / Spirit > Armour.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Weapons: The wand is the most important slot until 40. Path: Lesser and Greater Magic Wand (Enchanting), Sizzle Stick (15, WC), Gravestone Scepter (18, BFD), Charred Wand (19, Hillsbrad), Dancing Flame (26, Arathi), Wand of Mana Concentration (27, Dalaran "Arcanic Enigma"), Wand of Eventide (27, bind-on-equip).

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Mistakes: Levelling as Holy, Psychic Scream that pulls extra mobs, Shadow Word: Death as a filler, Shadow before about 28 with no spell power, and not upgrading the wand.

statements.title: Priest (scope: forever)
statements.text: Solo/group: Shadow is solid solo, especially from 40, and a Shadow priest can heal every levelling dungeon. Priests find groups easily as healers.

statements.title: Priest (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: **✗** Classic opens with Wand Specialization 5/5 then Spirit Tap 5/5, but in Forever Wand Specialization costs 2 points and Spirit Tap may not exist.

statements.title: Priest (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: **✗ uncertain**: Classic ranks Spirit first because of Spirit Tap.

statements.title: Priest (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Train everything from 1 to 22, then be selective.

statements.title: Priest (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Don't reapply Shadow Word: Pain, don't Mind Blast mobs below 30% health, and don't overuse Shield.

statements.title: Priest (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: Spirit Tap needs the killing blow, so it is worth less in groups (if it exists in Forever).

statements.title: Priest (scope: classic_fallback)
statements.text: **✗** Classic Dwarf/Human-only Fear Ward and Desperate Prayer advice: Fear Ward is now baseline for every race.

statements.title: Paladin (scope: forever)
statements.text: Race: Human, Dwarf or Undead (Undead is new and the only Horde paladin race).

statements.title: Paladin (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Holy Strike is a new baseline instant at 6 that deals Holy damage on a 12-second cooldown (10 with Improved Holy Strike).

statements.title: Paladin (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Judgement no longer consumes the seal, its debuffs last 40 seconds, and it is off the global cooldown.

statements.title: Paladin (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Consecration and Blessing of Kings are baseline at 20. Consecration hits only 4 targets at full effect. Righteous Fury is trained at 10.

statements.title: Paladin (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Vengeance stacks to 5 and requires Seal of Command. Unsealed Wrath is a new 31-point talent that needs Repentance. Champion of the Light turns 10/20/30% of Intellect into spell damage. Conviction covers all spells and attacks.

statements.title: Paladin (scope: forever)
statements.text: Changes: Removed: Blessing of Light and Salvation, One-Handed Weapon Specialization and several "Improved" talents (Improved Blessing of Wisdom, Righteous Fury, Retribution Aura and Seal of the Crusader were made baseline). Divine Shield now halves your damage dealt. Lay on Hands has a 20-minute cooldown.

statements.title: Paladin (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Retribution is the consensus levelling spec. Protection is an option for pulls of about 4 mobs with Consecration. Shockadin/Holy is for duo play.

statements.title: Paladin (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Retribution. The levelling build ends near 14/1/36; key talents and the level to have them by: Improved Judgement 2 by 18; Conviction 3 by 19; Seal of Command by 22; Sacred Arbiter by 26; Repentance by 33; Unsealed Wrath by 40.

statements.title: Paladin (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spec: Method instead opens with the mana talents (Benediction, Sanctified Judgement, Improved Judgement) and takes Pursuit of Justice as early as possible (15% speed).

statements.title: Paladin (scope: forever)
statements.text: Spells: Key levels: Seal of Righteousness, Holy Light and Devotion Aura 1; Blessing of Might and Judgement 4; Holy Strike 6; Hammer of Justice 8; Blessing of Protection, Lay on Hands, Seal of Fury and Righteous Fury 10; Consecration, Exorcism, Flash of Light, Blessing of Kings and Polearms 20; Divine Intervention 30; Divine Shield 32.

statements.title: Paladin (scope: forever)
statements.text: Rotation: 1–20: Seal of Righteousness, Judgement as you close in, Holy Strike, with Judgement and Holy Strike on cooldown. From 20 with a two-hander: Seal of Command, Judgement, Holy Strike, Hammer of Wrath below 20% health. Use Consecration sparingly.

statements.title: Paladin (scope: forever)
